subject: Moonbeam — committed capacity absorption & SLO sensitivity modeling
messages:

Cc: Procurement <procurement@moonbeam.ai>, Harrison Cole <ctoharrison@moonbeam.ai>

Subject: Dedicated commit sizing — initial data and ask

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. CTO asked us to move faster on a committed capacity proposal so we can evaluate pricing for a 12–18 month commit. We've attached a short sample of our traffic (initial_usage_samples.csv) showing daily peaks and a couple of 15-minute bursts. High level: average token/sec during business hours is ~75k, bursts up to ~480k for ~3–6 minutes, and our 99th-percentile request size is ~420 tokens.

Two asks: can Redwood run a short absorption / sensitivity model to show how a Dedicated slab (8 vs 12 GPUs) maps to p95/p99 latency for a 70B-class model (quantized) and recommend headroom for a commit? Also please outline what typical buffers you recommend for bursty workloads like ours.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants a recommended commit tier to price.

Best,
Alice Nguyen
Head of Infrastructure
Moonbeam AI
[Attachment: initial_usage_samples.csv (text/csv)]

Alice — thanks, got the samples. Looping Ben (serving runtime) and Evelyn (solutions) to run the simulation and surface a short, readable recommendation for Procurement.

Quick sketch from my side so Procurement has something to work with immediately:
- Workload baseline: business-hours steady-state ~75k tokens/sec.
- Observed short bursts: up to 480k tps for ~3–6 minutes (we'll model 5-min sustained for worst-case).
- Median request length: ~180 tokens; 99th ~420 tokens — impacts KV cache efficacy on chat-style flows.

Rough runway estimate (back-of-envelope): with our quantized 70B family and continuous batching, a single A100-equivalent GPU slab can sustain ~45k–60k tokens/sec steady-state depending on batch mix and KV cache hit rates. That implies 2–3 GPUs for the steady-state, but bursts require slab-level headroom.

Action items: Ben will attach a spreadsheet with tokens->GPU math and SLO sensitivity curves. Evelyn will draft recommended commit slab (and recommended cushion %) and the procurement-friendly phrasing for the contract.

I'll follow up with timing — aiming for an internal note + slide for you by tomorrow EOD PT.

—Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice@moonbeam.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — initial data and ask (model run + attachments)

Jonas / Alice — attaching the modeling workbook (moonbeam_compute_profile.xlsx) and a short SLO-tail note (slo_tail_analysis.pdf). Below is an executive summary and the key calculations so procurement can see assumptions quickly.

Executive summary:
- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 350 ms for generation requests (70B quantized, 8-token-condense prompt patterns).
- Steady-state (75k tps) -> modeled to require 3 GPUs (A100-eq) at 70% utilization for the request mix we saw (mix includes ~25% short queries, 60% medium, 15% long).
- Burst sizing: a 5-minute sustained burst at 480k tps cannot be absorbed by a 3-GPU slab. We modeled slabs at 6, 8, 10, 12 GPUs.

Key numbers (selected):
- Per-GPU sustained capacity (mixed workload, conservative batching): 55k tokens/sec (median case).
- Estimated p95 latency mapping (approx):
  - 6 GPUs (330k cap) -> steady p95 = ~420 ms (miss SLO), p99 >> 500ms
  - 8 GPUs (440k cap) -> steady p95 = ~360 ms (near SLO), 99th ~480ms for 5-min sustained bursts
  - 10 GPUs (550k cap) -> steady p95 = ~320 ms (meets SLO with ~10–15% headroom), 99th ~400ms

Recommendation for a 12–18 month commit:
- Commit slab: 10 GPUs. Rationale: covers observed 480k peak with modest headroom for routing variation and KV-cache warmup (we assume 10% drop in effective capacity during cold-starts or multi-tenant noise).
- Operational cushion: add burstable pool of 2 GPUs (dedicated burst buffer) or allow on-demand overflow in the Hosted pool for short bursts. That yields effective peak absorption ~650k tps for short windows when combined with autoscaling/burst-capacity rules.
- Policy suggestion: define \"Burst window\" for pricing (e.g., up to 10 minutes/day at on-demand rates) to avoid overcommitting for rare spikes.

Short math snippet used in workbook (columns deliberately rounded in sheet):
- required_gpus = ceil(peak_tokens_per_sec / per_gpu_capacity)
- per_gpu_capacity used = 55_000 * (1 - cache_miss_rate) * (1 - safety_factor)
- safety_factor baseline = 0.10 (10% for ops noise)

Assumptions / sensitivity to call out to Moonbeam:
- If KV cache hit-rate is >80% (chat with warm prefixes), per-GPU effective capacity increases ~20% -> 8 GPUs would be sufficient.
- If median request length shifts upward (more 1k+ token calls), capacity per GPU drops significantly; we'd re-run with actual token-length distribution.
- Tail behavior (p99) is sensitive to batching windows and concurrency knobs; we show p99 curves in the attached PDF.

I've included scenario tabs in the workbook: baseline, optimistic cache, pessimistic cold-start, and burst-only. Evelyn: feel free to pull the short bullet list for procurement.

Attachments: [Attachment: moonbeam_compute_profile.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)], [Attachment: slo_tail_analysis.pdf (application/pdf)]

—Ben
Sr. Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

Jonas — thanks for the quick analysis. Procurement and finance want two pieces to proceed: (1) a clear recommended commit slab and expected monthly unit price (or range) for the 12-month commit; (2) suggested contract language for burst allowances (we prefer a simple bucket rather than per-minute billing complexity).

Can you provide a one-page summary with the recommended slab (you suggested 10 GPUs + 2 burstable), an expected monthly committed price range, and a recommended \"burst bucket\" definition? We can then circulate a term sheet internally.

Also looping Harrison (CTO) for a quick read.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Moonbeam AI

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 9 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing — initial data and ask

Procurement — thanks, will do. Short answer here while we prep the one-pager:
- Recommended commit: 10 dedicated GPUs (A100-equivalent) reserved slab + 2-GPU burst buffer (dedicated) OR explicit overflow to Hosted at published on-demand rates.
- Suggested burst bucket: 60 GPU-minutes/day (allocatable in 5-minute increments), or equivalently 10 minutes/day at full 6-GPU burst capacity; unused minutes do not roll over. We find this simple bucket aligns incentives and keeps pricing predictable.
- Expected pricing (range): we will provide a firm monthly committed price in the one-pager, but ballpark: $X/month–$Y/month depending on exchange rate and support SLA (this will be replaced by a dollar figure in the official quote).

Next steps: Ben and I will produce a single-page procurement-friendly summary and a short slide with the sensitivity chart by EOD PT tomorrow; Alice, what time is best for a 20–30 minute review?

—Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
